title: Wallabag test allows authenticated SSRF to arbitrary HTTP(S) targets

evidence.quote:

reasoning: The stored Wallabag URL is only constrained to start with http:// or https://. The test route then performs a server-side POST to that configured URL and follows redirects. Any client with the API key can use this route to make the server connect to localhost, private IPs, cloud metadata hosts, or redirect chains, which crosses the network/user-input trust boundary. The API key requirement limits exposure but does not make the outbound request safe.
reproduction: With a valid API key, PUT /api/config/wallabag with url set to http://127.0.0.1:8080 and non-empty credential fields, then POST /api/config/wallabag/test. The server attempts to connect to http://127.0.0.1:8080/oauth/v2/token.
recommendation: Validate Wallabag URLs with the existing public-URL safety policy before saving and before outbound requests, block private/loopback/link-local/reserved hosts unless explicitly allowed, reject userinfo, and re-check redirect targets or disable redirects for this token request.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no linked tests for POST /wallabag/test, and no Wallabag API tests were found that assert private or loopback URLs are rejected before outbound network access.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests that reject localhost, 127.0.0.1, private RFC1918 addresses, and redirect-to-private targets for Wallabag connection testing.
minimumFixScope: Wallabag URL validation in app/api/config.py and outbound request safety in app/services/wallabag_service.py.
